choices.text: Nothing - after five heads, tails really is more likely than heads
The student is right about the direction but wrong about the size of the effect
Tosses are independent: the coin never remembers, so the next toss is still 1/2 tails
Heads is now more likely, because the coin is on a hot streak

questions.explanation: The trap claim is: After five heads in a row, tails is due. A long run feels like it must balance out. But tosses are independent: The coin never remembers: after five heads the next toss is still 1/2. A run of five heads was unlikely before it started - probability 1/32 - yet once it has happened it changes nothing about toss six.
questions.misconception: After five heads in a row, tails is due.
questions.prompt: A student tosses a fair coin, gets five heads in a row, and says the next toss is more likely to be tails because tails is due. What is wrong with that claim?

choices.text: 2, the largest value X can take

questions.explanation: Expectation weights each value by its probability: E(X) = 0(0.2) + 1(0.5) + 2(0.3) = 0 + 0.5 + 0.6 = 1.1. It is the balance point of the distribution, not a value X ever takes.
questions.prompt: A discrete random variable X takes values 0, 1, 2 with probabilities 0.2, 0.5, 0.3. What is E(X)?

questions.answer: 0.3. The probabilities in a discrete distribution sum to 1, so P(X = 2) = 1 - 0.2 - 0.5 = 0.3.
questions.explanation: Every discrete probability distribution sums to exactly 1 because something has to happen: 1 - 0.2 - 0.5 = 0.3. Checking the sum first also catches invalid tables before any further work.
questions.prompt: A probability table for X lists P(X = 0) = 0.2 and P(X = 1) = 0.5, with X = 2 the only other outcome. Find P(X = 2) and state the rule you used.

questions.prompt: Let X be the number of successes in 10 independent trials, each with success probability 0.3. Write down the formula for P(X = 3) and evaluate it.

choices.text: About 68%, because 40 to 60 is one standard deviation each side
About 99.7%, because the interval looks wide
About 95%, because 40 and 60 are two standard deviations from the mean
About 50%, because half the curve lies above the mean

questions.explanation: 40 = 50 - 2(5) and 60 = 50 + 2(5), so the interval reaches two standard deviations each side of the mean. The 68-95-99.7 rule gives about 95% within two standard deviations.
questions.prompt: A normal distribution has mean 50 and standard deviation 5. Using the 68-95-99.7 rule, about what proportion of values lie between 40 and 60?
